hypothesis: For a well-scoped, low-risk support workflow (e.g., triaging and responding to low-complexity customer emails about billing or account status), a single production-grade agent integrated with the ticketing system and guarded by human-in-the-loop approvals will (a) reduce median handling time per request by at least 40%, (b) reduce direct handling labor cost per request by at least 30%, and (c) maintain or improve response quality (no statistically significant degradation in correctness or tone as assessed by blinded reviewers) relative to the current manual process.

baseline.description: Current-state manual processing of low-complexity customer support emails (e.g., billing questions, plan questions, address changes) performed by human agents using the production ticketing/CRM system.

entry_criteria: Inbound request arrives via a monitored support email inbox (e.g., support@company.com) or web form.

The request is automatically or manually tagged as belonging to the selected starter workflow (e.g., 'billing-simple', 'account-update') based on simple rules (keyword filters) and does not require cross-team escalation.
The request is in the primary language supported by the support team (e.g., English).
steps: 1. Human agent reads the inbound email or web form submission.
2. Human agent searches internal knowledge base / SOPs and, if needed, the CRM/billing system for the customer record.
3. Human agent determines the appropriate response, including any simple account lookups or updates permitted in this workflow.
4. Human agent composes a response email in the ticketing system, optionally using existing templates.
5. Human agent submits the response, resolves or updates ticket status, and logs relevant metadata (tags, category, resolution code).
exit_criteria: Customer has received a response via email or portal message.
Ticket is updated with resolution code and any relevant notes.
No additional human actions are required unless the customer replies again (which would create or reopen a ticket outside the primary measurement window).

roles: Support team lead (responsible for quality sampling and baseline metrics collection).
experience_requirements: Agents participating in the baseline measurement must have at least 30 days of experience handling this workflow to avoid ramp-up bias.

measurement_window.duration: At least 2 full business weeks OR until a minimum of 200 qualifying tickets are processed, whichever is longer.
stability_conditions: No major product releases, pricing changes, or policy changes that substantially alter the nature of incoming requests during the baseline period.
No significant staffing disruptions (e.g., more than 30% of shifts staffed by temporary workers unfamiliar with the process).

required_fields_per_ticket: Ticket category / tag indicating the starter workflow (e.g., 'billing-simple').
optional_fields: Customer satisfaction score (if available, e.g., post-ticket CSAT survey).
Internal quality review score (if existing QA program is in place).

data_collection_method.description: Use ticketing system exports or API to retrieve raw ticket data for the defined measurement window, then filter by entry criteria to form the baseline dataset.
artifacts: Anonymized sample of request/response texts (redacted PII) for quality evaluation.
Documentation of any filtering or cleaning logic used.

treatment.description: Single production-grade agent that triages and drafts responses for the same low-complexity customer support workflow, integrated with the ticketing/CRM system and subject to human-in-the-loop review before sending responses.

agent_design.role_definition: Customer Support Drafting Agent for simple billing and account-related inquiries. The agent reads incoming requests, retrieves necessary context (customer profile, subscription data, knowledge base articles), and proposes a structured resolution and response draft for human approval.

tools.name: ticketing_api
capabilities: Read ticket metadata and full message text.
constraints: Agent cannot directly send external replies via this tool; it can only save drafts or internal notes.

tools.name: crm_billing_api
capabilities: Lookup customer by email or account ID.
Read subscription status, invoices, and simple account attributes.
Read-only access only for this experiment; no write/update actions.

tools.name: kb_search_api
capabilities: Retrieve relevant knowledge base articles or standard operating procedures based on query text.

context_inputs: Relevant historical tickets for the customer (optional, limited to last N).
Current policy constraints for this workflow (e.g., maximum allowed credit, data you may not expose).

requires_handover.description: True if the agent determines that this request is outside its allowed workflow scope.

resolution_plan.description: Short natural language explanation of what information was used and what resolution is proposed.

response_draft.description: Customer-facing email body draft, following tone and policy guidelines.

tool_actions.description: List of suggested non-destructive tool calls (e.g., KB links to attach, internal note suggestions). In this experiment, actual state-changing tool calls in production systems are disabled or stubbed.

confidence.description: Agent's self-reported confidence in the proposed resolution.

review_ui_requirements: Provide text editor for modifying response_draft.
Buttons for the four review modes, with required reason on reject/redirect.
approval_policy: All agent-generated responses in the experimental cohort must be explicitly approved by a human before being sent to customers.
If the human chooses 'reject_and_handle_manually' or 'redirect_out_of_scope', the agent's draft is not sent; the human composes and sends a new reply.
If the human materially edits the response (e.g., more than a configurable character threshold), this is recorded in the experiment log.

phases.name: Shadow Mode (Optional but Recommended)
phases.description: Agent runs in the background and generates drafts that are not visible to the support agent. Used to validate correctness offline.
phases.duration: At least 100 tickets or 3 business days for sanity checks.

phases.name: Assist Mode (Primary Experimental Phase)
phases.description: Agent-generated drafts are presented to support agents who must review, edit if necessary, and approve or reject.
phases.traffic_allocation: At least 50% of eligible tickets routed to agent-assisted lane; remaining eligible tickets handled manually as concurrent control if possible.

required_fields_per_ticket: Agent request timestamp (when agent is invoked for drafting).
Agent response timestamp (when structured output is returned).
Human first-view timestamp (when a support agent sees the draft).
Review mode selected (approve_as_is, edit_then_approve, reject_and_handle_manually, redirect_out_of_scope).
Edit distance or a proxy metric between agent response_draft and final sent response.
Any human comments/labels about agent errors (optional, for richer diagnostics).
logging_requirements: Persist full structured output from agent (with PII redacted for analysis logs).
Persist snapshot of context inputs passed to agent (ticket text, KB snippets metadata, CRM summary), with sensitive data either removed or tokenized.
Record model configuration (model name, version, temperature, tool config) per invocation.

workloads.name: Low-Complexity Billing and Account Inquiries
workloads.description: Customer emails or tickets asking for simple billing and account information that can be answered using read-only access to CRM/billing data and standard policies.
examples: “Can you send me a copy of my last invoice?”
“What plan am I currently on and when does my subscription renew?”
“I need to update the billing address on my account.”
“Was my last payment received? I want to make sure my account is active.”
inclusion_criteria: Tickets tagged by existing rules or simple heuristics as belonging to 'billing-simple' or 'account-info' categories.
No evidence of complex dispute, refund, or fraud investigation in the request.
Single-customer context (no multi-account or complex organizational hierarchies needed).
exclusion_criteria: Requests involving refunds, discounts, credits, or pricing negotiations.
Requests indicating legal action, complaints, or escalations.
Requests requiring changes in backend billing data in this initial experiment (read-only integrations only).

normalization_steps: Strip signatures and legal footers where feasible using heuristic rules.
Retain original spelling and grammar errors.
Preserve timestamps and threading metadata but pass only the most recent customer message to the agent by default, with prior context available as needed.

randomization.method: For each eligible incoming ticket, randomly assign to baseline_manual or treatment_agentic lane with a fixed probability (e.g., 50/50), subject to capacity constraints.
implementation_notes: Randomization can be implemented as a stateless hash on ticket ID modulo 2, or via a simple random number generator at routing time.
Ensure that the same customer is not systematically biased to one lane by seeding randomization with ticket ID, not customer ID.

concurrency.description: Where possible, operate baseline and treatment concurrently to avoid time-based confounds (e.g., seasonal ticket volume, policy changes).
concurrency.fallback: If concurrent operation is not possible, collect baseline and treatment sequentially under documented, comparable conditions, and avoid overlapping with major events (e.g., new feature launches).

agent_configuration_lock.description: Lock key agent parameters during the core experimental window.
locked_parameters: Prompt templates for system and agent instructions.
change_management: Any mid-experiment changes to prompts, tools, or model versions must be recorded with timestamps and used to define pre-change and post-change segments.
Primary analysis should focus on periods with stable configuration.

instructions_to_agents: Manual-lane support staff should follow existing SOPs and not adopt agent-like drafting behaviors introduced solely for the experiment.
Agentic-lane support staff should be instructed to use the agent drafts but are free to edit or reject based on their judgment.
Staff should not preferentially route easier or harder tickets to one lane outside the randomized assignment.
training: Provide a short, standardized training for all participating support agents on how to interact with the agent interface, including when to reject drafts.
Document training materials and attendance to ensure consistent instruction.

pii_handling: Production systems will still handle PII as usual; for analysis and repository examples, all PII must be redacted or synthetic.
Logs exported for analysis must replace any direct identifiers (names, emails, account IDs) with consistent pseudonyms or hashes.
scope_limits: Agent has read-only access to CRM/billing APIs in this experiment; no write operations to financial systems.
Agent cannot directly send external communications; only drafts that humans may approve and send.

metrics.name: handling_time_first_response
metrics.definition: Time from ticket creation to first meaningful response sent to the customer (manual lane) or approved agent draft sent to the customer (agentic lane).

metrics.name: agent_draft_latency
metrics.definition: Time from agent request timestamp to agent structured output being available. Only applicable to agentic lane.

metrics.name: labor_time_per_ticket
metrics.definition: Estimated total human working time per ticket. For manual lane, approximated by time window between agent opening ticket and resolving it, adjusted by concurrency assumptions; for agentic lane, measured as review and editing time plus any manual actions.

metrics.name: labor_cost_per_ticket
metrics.definition: Labor_time_per_ticket multiplied by fully-loaded hourly cost of support agents, divided by 3600.

metrics.name: model_cost_per_ticket
metrics.definition: Estimated LLM and associated API costs per ticket in the agentic lane, based on token usage and provider pricing.

metrics.name: total_variable_cost_per_ticket
metrics.definition: Sum of labor_cost_per_ticket and model_cost_per_ticket. For baseline/manual, model_cost_per_ticket is zero.

metrics.name: first_touch_resolution_rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of tickets resolved with a single customer interaction (no follow-up from customer within a defined window, e.g., 48 hours).

metrics.name: csat_score
metrics.unit: score (0–100 or 1–5, depending on existing system)
metrics.definition: Average post-interaction customer satisfaction score for tickets in the experiment, where available.

metrics.name: qa_correctness_score
metrics.definition: Blinded reviewer judgment of factual and policy correctness of the response for a stratified random sample of tickets.
scale: 0.5 = partially correct or minor issues, but overall acceptable.
0.0 = incorrect or policy-violating; would need rework.

metrics.name: qa_tone_score
metrics.definition: Blinded reviewer assessment that the tone meets company guidelines for professionalism and empathy, using the same 0/0.5/1 scale as correctness.

metrics.name: agent_draft_accept_rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of agent-generated drafts that are approved_as_is or edit_then_approve (vs. reject_and_handle_manually or redirect_out_of_scope).

metrics.name: agent_draft_minor_edit_rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of approved drafts where the human edit distance stays below a defined threshold (e.g., <20% of characters changed), indicating near-ready quality.

metrics.name: out_of_scope_rate
metrics.definition: Fraction of tickets initially routed to the agentic lane that end up redirected_out_of_scope or requiring manual takeover.

metrics.name: error_incident_count
metrics.definition: Number of documented incidents where the agent draft, if not corrected by humans, would have caused a materially incorrect or policy-breaching response, as flagged by reviewers or agents.

primary.target: Median handling_time_first_response in the agentic lane is at least 40% lower than in the manual lane.
primary.formal_test: Mann-Whitney U test on ticket-level handling_time_first_response; p < 0.05 for difference in distributions in the desired direction.

primary.target: Mean total_variable_cost_per_ticket in the agentic lane is at least 30% lower than in the manual lane.
primary.formal_test: Two-sample t-test (or non-parametric bootstrap) on mean costs; p < 0.05.

primary.target: No statistically significant decrease in qa_correctness_score for agentic responses versus manual, within a margin of -0.05 on a 0–1 scale.
primary.formal_test: Equivalence test (TOST) with lower bound = -0.05, upper bound = +0.05; p < 0.05 for equivalence.

secondary.target: No statistically significant degradation; ideally improvement.
secondary.analysis: Descriptive statistics plus equivalence or non-inferiority test with margin -0.05.

secondary.target: At least 70% of agent drafts are accepted (approve_as_is or edit_then_approve).
At least 40% of approved drafts require only minor edits (<20% of characters changed).
No more than a small, predefined tolerance (e.g., < 1% of tickets in agentic lane have serious potential errors not caught by reviewers).

stopping_rules: If during the experiment more than N serious potential incidents (e.g., policy violations, security breaches) are identified over M tickets (e.g., > 3 over 200 tickets), pause the experiment and perform a safety review.
If qa_correctness_score in agentic lane falls below manual lane by more than 0.1 (absolute) in interim checks, temporarily halt new ticket routing to agentic lane and investigate.

failure_modes.name: Scope Creep and Misclassification
failure_modes.description: Tickets outside the intended low-risk workflow are routed to the agent, leading to poor drafts or escalations.
indicators: Qualitative feedback that many drafts are irrelevant.
mitigations: Tighten routing rules to the starter workflow.
Refine system prompt to more aggressively decline uncertain requests.
Introduce a preliminary classifier (simple rules or ML model) as a gatekeeper.

failure_modes.name: Quality Drift Over Time
failure_modes.description: Agent performance changes due to upstream model updates, KB changes, or silent prompt edits.
indicators: Week-over-week degradation in qa_correctness_score or agent_draft_accept_rate.
mitigations: Version and lock models/prompts for the duration of the main measurement period.
Add automated regression checks on a fixed evaluation set after any change in upstream dependencies.

failure_modes.name: Human Over-Editing or Over-Reliance
failure_modes.description: Some agents heavily edit every draft (eliminating time savings), while others over-trust drafts without sufficient review.
indicators: Bimodal distribution in edit distances per reviewer.
Inconsistent qa scores across different human reviewers.
mitigations: Standardize guidance on acceptable edits and review rigor.
Run calibration sessions where reviewers score sample drafts together.

failure_modes.name: Biased Sampling or Non-Comparable Cohorts
failure_modes.description: Manual and agentic lanes serve systematically different kinds of tickets, invalidating comparisons.
indicators: Different distributions of ticket sub-categories or customer segments across lanes.
Different times-of-day or days-of-week patterns per lane.
mitigations: Use randomized assignment at ticket level.
Weight results or stratify analyses by ticket type and time window.
If manual routing overrides occur, log them and analyze impact.

failure_modes.name: Instrumentation Gaps
failure_modes.description: Missing or inaccurate timestamps, IDs, or flags make it impossible to compute key metrics reliably.
indicators: Null or inconsistent values for experiment flags in exports.
Mismatch between ticket counts in source system and analysis dataset.
mitigations: Run dry-runs and validation queries before starting full experiment.
Implement schema validation checks on logs (e.g., required fields not null).
Automate daily sanity checks on metric aggregates.

systems: Ticketing or helpdesk platform with API access (e.g., Zendesk, Freshdesk, ServiceNow, or similar).
CRM/billing system with read-only API access for relevant customer and subscription fields.
Knowledge base or documentation repository with search API or export capability.
LLM provider or in-house model endpoint capable of running the agent prompts and tools.
Logging and analytics stack (e.g., data warehouse, log aggregation, metrics dashboard) to store and analyze experiment data.
access_and_permissions: Service account(s) for ticketing and CRM systems with least-privilege, read-only permissions for this experiment.
Credentials and network access for the LLM endpoint.
Permissions for the experiment team to create dashboards and export anonymized data for analysis.
datasets: Historical tickets dataset for baseline measurement and for designing prompts and evaluation samples (with PII redacted for repository examples).
Synthetic or sanitized ticket/response pairs to be included in the public GitHub repository for reproducibility.

synthetic_environment.description: For readers without access to production systems, a local/sandbox setup mimicking the workflow using synthetic tickets and stubbed APIs.
components: SQLite or local JSON files emulating ticketing, CRM, and KB data.
Python FastAPI or Flask app simulating the agent endpoint and HITL interface.
Docker compose file to spin up all necessary services locally.

run_instructions.title: Select and Document the Starter Workflow
actions: Choose a low-risk, high-volume, low-complexity support workflow (e.g., simple billing/account inquiries) following criteria in section 5.1.
Document entry/exit criteria and SOPs in a concise process spec file (e.g., experiments/ch05_first_production_agent/docs/workflow_spec.md).
Identify and tag historical tickets matching this workflow for baseline analysis.

run_instructions.title: Collect Baseline Data
actions: Export at least 200 historical tickets satisfying the workflow criteria with timestamps, agent IDs, and resolution codes.
Compute baseline metrics (handling_time_first_response, labor_time_per_ticket if possible, first_touch_resolution_rate, csat_score if available).
Optionally, run a small QA review of 30–50 baseline tickets to estimate qa_correctness_score and qa_tone_score under the current manual process.

run_instructions.title: Implement the Agent with Tools and Structured Outputs
actions: Implement agent.py using the specified structured_output_schema and tool interfaces from tools/*.py.
Define system and developer prompts embedding the workflow scope, safety constraints, and formatting requirements.
Test the agent offline on synthetic_tickets.csv to ensure it returns valid JSON outputs and plausible drafts.

run_instructions.title: Integrate with Ticketing and CRM Systems (or Stubs)
actions: Implement ticketing_client.py, crm_client.py, and kb_client.py with real API calls in production, or stubbed functions in the synthetic environment.
Ensure that in this experiment, CRM/billing API calls are read-only.
Create a routing script or webhook handler that invokes the agent when new eligible tickets are created.

run_instructions.title: Deploy Human-in-the-Loop Review Flow
actions: Implement hitl_ui_stub.py or integrate with your existing support console to display agent drafts alongside original tickets.
Add controls for approve_as_is, edit_then_approve, reject_and_handle_manually, redirect_out_of_scope, and capture the selected mode.
Train participating support agents on how to use the new interface and codify when to reject drafts (e.g., low confidence, out-of-scope, unclear answer).

run_instructions.title: Set Up Logging, Observability, and Metrics
actions: Ensure every ticket processed in either lane includes the required instrumentation fields (timestamps, lane flag, review mode, edit distance).
Configure logging to write structured JSON or Parquet logs to a centralized store.
Create a simple dashboard or notebook-based report to visualize key metrics daily (e.g., handling time distributions, accept rates).

run_instructions.title: Run Shadow Mode (Optional Validation)
actions: For the first 100–200 tickets, run the agent in shadow mode where drafts are not shown to support agents.
Randomly sample at least 50 shadow-mode tickets and have QA reviewers compare agent drafts against the actual manual responses.
If qa_correctness_score or qa_tone_score is substantially worse than manual (>0.1 difference), refine prompts/tools before moving to assist mode.

run_instructions.title: Run the Main Experiment (Assist Mode)
actions: Activate the assist mode where randomly selected eligible tickets are routed to the agentic lane.
Run the experiment for at least 2 weeks or until at least 200 tickets per lane are collected.
Monitor safety indicators daily (error_incident_count, severe QA flags) and apply stopping rules if necessary.

run_instructions.title: Sample and Evaluate Quality Blinded
actions: From each lane, randomly sample at least 50 tickets (or more if feasible).
Strip lane identifiers and present paired request/response to blinded reviewers following qa_guidelines.md.
Compute qa_correctness_score and qa_tone_score per lane and reviewer, then aggregate.

run_instructions.title: Analyze Results and Compare Manual vs. Agentic Performance
actions: Use analysis.ipynb or equivalent script to compute all defined metrics for both lanes.
Apply the statistical tests described in success_criteria where possible.
Summarize findings in a short report (e.g., experiments/ch05_first_production_agent/results/summary.md) including metric tables, charts, and interpretation relative to the hypothesis.

run_instructions.title: Decide on Next Steps and Productionization
actions: If success_criteria are met and failure_modes are within tolerances, plan to expand agent coverage (more tickets, more categories) and/or relax read-only constraints with appropriate safeguards.

If criteria are partially met (e.g., quality OK but cost savings low), identify bottlenecks (e.g., excessive human editing) and design follow-up experiments (prompt tuning, better tools, improved UI).
Document lessons learned and update organizational guidelines for designing additional production-ready agents.

agent_id.description: Identifier of the human support agent handling the ticket.

edit_distance_characters.description: Levenshtein distance between agent response_draft and final sent response.

edit_distance_ratio.description: Normalized edit distance (0–1), where 0 means no change and 1 means completely different.

human_comments.description: Optional free-text comments by the reviewer about the draft.

model_params.description: Model configuration such as temperature, max_tokens, etc.

storage_and_format.description: All evidence should be storable as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) or Parquet files with schemas matching the objects above.
files: logs/tickets.ndjson or tickets.parquet containing ticket_record entries.
logs/agent_interactions.ndjson or agent_interactions.parquet containing agent_interaction_record entries.
logs/qa_evaluations.ndjson or qa_evaluations.parquet containing qa_evaluation_record entries.
